issues.description: Patch is at least three patches mashed into one
issues.detail: This commit message says 'upload logs on crash' but the diff also: (1) reorders queue_msg vs pending_assignments in worker.py, (2) changes shutdown flush behavior in traces.py, (3) emits a new 'process_closed' event in proc_pool.py, (4) disables a test file and removes pytest -n auto in makefile, (5) adds pythonpath to pyproject. Each of those has a separate failure mode and a separate reason for being reverted. Split it. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry now mutates the root logger handlers behind everyone's back
issues.detail: The old code had a comment explaining force_flush deadlocks. The new code 'fixes' that by walking root.handlers and removing every LoggingHandler before flush. That's a global side effect on the user's logging configuration triggered from a telemetry shutdown path. If the user installed their own opentelemetry LoggingHandler for their own reasons, you just yanked it. At minimum only remove the handler this module installed; track it by identity, not by isinstance. This is BAD-TASTE — special-casing a class instead of owning your own handle.

issues.description: Disabling -n auto and silently dropping test_plugin_google_stt.py in the same diff
issues.detail: Turning off parallel test execution and removing a test file from CI is not a 'log upload' change. If google_stt is flaky, say so in its own commit with a reason. If -n auto is broken, say so in its own commit with a reason. Hiding two test-infra regressions inside a feature patch is exactly the kind of thing a maintainer six years from now will curse the author for when he is bisecting.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer searches root handlers by isinstance to find 'the' OTLP handler
issues.detail: Same anti-pattern as the shutdown change: iterate root logger handlers, isinstance-check for LoggingHandler, emit to the first one found, break. If there's more than one (including the user's own), behavior is undefined. The class that installs the handler in _setup_cloud_tracer knows what handler it installed — return it, store it, and replay into that specific object. Don't go fishing in global state.

issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is a plain list with no max size. If the job hangs for a while before crashing, or spins in a tight error loop logging at DEBUG, this grows without bound in the worker process. Cap it (ring buffer or maxlen), or at minimum document the assumed bound. A crash-log mechanism that itself causes OOM is worse than the bug it's solving.

issues.description: _on_cleanup calls init_recording with traces=False but logs=True and swallows exceptions
issues.detail: On the crash path, _on_cleanup constructs a RecordingOptions with logs=True and calls init_recording inside a bare 'except Exception'. Two problems: the import is done lazily inside the try (hiding ImportError at the wrong layer), and the exception handler calls _stop_log_buffering — but only on failure. On success, init_recording itself calls _flush_early_log_buffer(replay=True), which is fine, but the control flow is non-obvious: 'I am the cleanup path, I call init_recording which thinks it's the start path, which then flushes my buffer.' Document this or invert it so _on_cleanup calls the flush directly after wiring up the OTLP handler.

issues.description: init_recording early-return now has a side effect
issues.detail: Before this patch, 'if already initialized or not cloud: return' was a pure guard. Now it calls self._stop_log_buffering() in the same branch. The function's contract just changed silently: 'init_recording is idempotent' is still true for the caller, but now calling it twice tears down buffering you may have wanted. Pull this side effect out into the cleanup/setup path that actually owns the buffer lifecycle.

issues.description: Forcing _shutdown_fut from the done-callback can race with the normal shutdown path
issues.detail: _on_entry_done now does set_result on _shutdown_fut whenever the job task raises. contextlib.suppress(InvalidStateError) papers over the race with anything else that may have set the future. That's fine for the not-yet-set case, but in the path where the job raised after partial connect, you may be racing the normal shutdown writer. Audit the writers of _shutdown_fut and make the precedence explicit; don't lean on InvalidStateError as control flow.

issues.description: process_closed emitted on init-failure path was not emitted before — verify subscriber assumptions
issues.detail: _proc_spawn_task now emits 'process_closed' when initialization fails. Existing subscribers may have assumed 'process_closed' implies 'process previously initialized / had a pid'. The test diff confirms this: 'if proc.pid is not None: pids.append(proc.pid)' had to be added because proc.pid can now be None at close time. Any other listener anywhere in the codebase or in user code with the same assumption is now silently broken. Document the event contract change in the commit message at minimum.

issues.description: worker.py reorder of _queue_msg and pending_assignments is unexplained
issues.detail: The diff swaps the order of 'await self._queue_msg(availability_resp)' and registering wait_assignment in _pending_assignments. This looks like a real fix for a race (server could send assignment before we register the future), but it's buried in a log-upload PR with no commit message. If it is a race fix, it deserves its own commit and its own test. If it isn't, revert it.

issues.description: Naming: _on_entry_done is fine, but the comment 'force it to trigger shutdown so _on_cleanup can flush crash logs' belongs in the commit message
issues.detail: The mechanism is non-obvious enough that the inline comment is doing real work. Good. But the linkage between 'force shutdown_fut' here and 'init_recording from _on_cleanup' over in job.py is the actual design of this patch and should be in the commit message, not split across two file-local comments.

from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions is done inside a try inside _on_cleanup. If this is to break a circular import, fine — say so in a comment. Otherwise hoist it. Lazy imports buried in error paths are a classic way for an ImportError to only manifest in production crash handling.

review.summary: The underlying idea is sound: buffer logs early, flush them through OTLP on crash so we can actually debug failures before session.start(). That's a real problem worth solving. But this patch is at least three patches stapled together — the log-buffering feature, a worker.py race reorder, a telemetry shutdown rework, a proc_pool event contract change, and an unrelated test-infra retreat (disabling -n auto, dropping a test file). Each of those deserves its own diff with its own reason. Inside the feature itself, the BAD-TASTE issue is the same pattern in two places: walk the root logger's handlers, isinstance-check, mutate. Own your handle, don't fish for it. NEEDS-WORK: split into separate commits, track installed OTLP handlers by identity not type, cap the buffer, and pull the side effect out of init_recording's early-return.
